clue.text: Girl pursuing 22, perhaps only after profit

indicators.note: the girl follows behind the other piece, as a pursuer comes after

parts.note: 22 points to Catch-22, the novel, so the number stands for the word catch
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl chasing after some number has her eye only on the money.
explanation.walkthrough: '22, perhaps' is a cross-reference trap: it does not mean entry 22 but the number in Joseph Heller's title Catch-22.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny describes something cheap and showy made merely to make money, so it is only after profit.

clue.text: Briefly very good in bed? Suffer the consequences!

indicators.note: in places the short word for very good inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a child's bed
pi is a short form of pious, very good in a sanctimonious way

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for being too good between the sheets and warned of the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is crossword shorthand for pious, read here as 'very good'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop it is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished, suffering the consequences.

clue.text: Kit partly recorded songs out in Amsterdam

parts.note: tracks are songs on a recording
uit is the Dutch word for out

explanation.surface: Part of a team's gear was recorded songs released in Amsterdam.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is athletic clothing, forming part of a sports kit.

clue.text: Put up with diet? It rules out the majority of parties

definitions.text: It rules out the majority of parties

parts.note: hung means put up, as a picture on a wall
a Diet is the name of a national assembly, as in Japan

explanation.surface: Tolerating a strict eating plan rules out most celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with diet' looks like tolerating a slimming regime; 'with' just joins. A hung parliament is one where no party has an overall majority.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hung parliament no single party holds a majority of seats, so a majority for any party is ruled out.

clue.text: Reserve a spot where The Ring may be put on?

parts.words: where The Ring may be put on
parts.note: an ear is where a ring may be put on, or where Wagner's Ring cycle is heard
a mark is a spot

explanation.surface: Book a place at an opera house where Wagner's Ring cycle may be staged.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic The Ring suggests Wagner's opera, put on at a theatre; here it is an earring worn on an EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds or items is to set them aside for a purpose, reserving them.

clue.text: Starts to turn on dubious type of power supply

indicators.note: the starts, the two opening letters, change round, so the first letter moves behind the second

parts.note: unclear means dubious or uncertain

explanation.surface: Begin switching on a questionable form of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to turn on' swaps the first two letters of UNCLEAR; 'on' joins to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power, from atomic reactors, is a type of energy supply.

clue.text: Very keen pupil pulls back

indicators.note: back signals that the word for pulls is read from end to start

parts.note: to tow is to pull, so pulls gives tows

explanation.surface: An eager student tugs something backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is British slang for a student who studies very hard, an eager pupil.

clue.text: Third of drivers nicked, pulled up for behaving erratically?

indicators.note: in a down entry up signals reading the whole from bottom to top
nicked means stolen, so the pulled word takes in the letter

parts.note: drew means pulled, as a cart

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of drivers

explanation.surface: A third of motorists caught by police and stopped for driving erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' looks like arrested; here DREW 'nicks' the I, giving DRIEW, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird means odd or strange, the adjective for something behaving erratically.

clue.text: One on the staff seemed to hold old woman up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the combination is read bottom to top
to hold means the seemed word surrounds the old woman

parts.note: felt means seemed, as in 'it felt wrong'
a crone is an old woman

explanation.surface: An employee seemed to hold up an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees; it is the musical stave on which a clef sits. 'to hold' and 'up' (reversal in a down clue) make the reading run bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor clef is a sign placed on a musical stave, a symbol sitting on the staff.

clue.text: Popular, unlikely to fail, and upright

explanation.surface: A well-liked, reliable and honest person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good standing means being well regarded, reliable in credit and respectable, so each sense fits.

clue.text: Left to make entry in serious critic's diary, perhaps

indicators.note: making entry in means going inside, so the letter for left is placed within the critic

parts.note: a critic who pans everything is a panner, a severe reviewer

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to write an entry in a stern reviewer's journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary used to schedule appointments is a kind of organiser, an example of the defined item.

clue.text: Hand over 25 evidence

parts.note: entry 25 is the word meaning opposed, whose short synonym is con, as in pros and cons
a sign is evidence or an indication of something

explanation.surface: Pass on twenty-five pieces of proof.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 25 refers to the answer at 25 across, meaning 'opposed to'; its synonym CON supplies the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to hand them over to someone's care or delivery.

clue.text: Happen to see part of proposed film set

parts.note: a take is a single filmed shot, a part of a film being made
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Chance to look at a section of a planned movie's studio set.
explanation.definitionFit: To take place means to occur, a plain synonym for happen.

clue.text: Type of column in demand

definitions.meaning: in architecture Doric, Ionic and Corinthian are classical styles of column
to demand something is to command it

explanation.surface: A kind of pillar requested.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric and Ionic are classical orders of architecture; an order is also a command or demand.

clue.text: Obscure across clue — finally getting more down

indicators.note: across here means spanning, so the blur word stretches over the letter

parts.note: to obscure is to blur

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of clue

explanation.surface: A puzzle solver finds an across clue baffling and ends up feeling lower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' looks like the crossword direction but means BLUR lies across (around) the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad, so bluer is sadder, more down in spirits.

clue.text: Push for renewed progress in the motoring business

definitions.text: Push for renewed progress in the motoring business

parts.words: Push for renewed progress in the motoring business
parts.note: describes shoving a stalled car so its engine catches, not a campaign for growth in the car trade

explanation.surface: A drive to revive the car industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a business campaign; the motoring sense is starting a car by pushing it and engaging the clutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump start is starting a car by pushing it and letting the clutch in, a push to get going again.

clue.text: This precaution could be taken — if on edge, by the way

definitions.text: This precaution could be taken — if on edge, by the way

parts.words: This precaution could be taken — if on edge, by the way
parts.note: a safety routine practised by children standing at the edge of the pavement beside the road before crossing

explanation.surface: Someone nervous takes a safety measure while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' suggests nerves but means standing at the pavement's edge; 'by the way' means beside the road. A KERB is the British spelling of the pavement edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The kerb drill is the British road-safety routine of looking both ways from the pavement edge before crossing.

clue.text: Copying that's about with German's. Life of Caesar brought up?

indicators.note: about means the that's letters surround the rest

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
mit is German for with

indicators.note: in a down entry brought up means the Latin word is read bottom to top

parts.note: vita is Latin, Caesar's language, for life

explanation.surface: Imitating a biography of Caesar written in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life of Caesar' looks like a book title; it is the Latin word VITA, reversed to ATIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitative means copying or mimicking something else.

clue.text: Lose pounds in weight, say

parts.note: read as dieting, but meaning to abandon imperial units such as pounds for kilograms

explanation.surface: Someone wants to shed a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests slimming; the real sense is converting measurements from imperial to the decimal system.
explanation.definitionFit: To metricate is to convert to metric units, so pounds in weight are dropped in favour of kilograms.

clue.text: Most "astrally" cast?

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new arrangement, signalling the letters are rearranged
most of the word means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Which cast is the most star-filled?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' drops the Y of ASTRALLY; 'cast' rearranges ASTRALL. The whole describes the starriest cast.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast is made up entirely of celebrities, the most starry cast possible.

clue.text: Item raised in somewhat suprising circumstances

definitions.text: Item raised in somewhat suprising circumstances

parts.words: Item raised in somewhat suprising circumstances
parts.note: describes a part of the face lifted when one is a little surprised, not a matter raised at a meeting

explanation.surface: A point brought up at an unexpected moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item raised' suggests a topic brought up; it is a facial feature lifted in mild surprise. 'suprising' is the setter's own misspelling.
explanation.definitionFit: People raise an eyebrow when mildly surprised, so this facial feature is lifted in such moments.

clue.text: One's inclined to take linked article provided

indicators.note: linked says the article and the condition word are woven together rather than set side by side

parts.note: the is the definite article
if means provided, as in 'if it rains'

explanation.surface: Someone tends to accept a connected item that is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked' interlocks THE and IF: T, H, then I, E, F alternate, which here means moving THE's E one place on.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is a person disposed to take what is not theirs, someone inclined to steal.

clue.text: Involved in swindle, right to beat hasty retreat

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the letter for right goes into the swindle

parts.note: a scam is a swindle

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a fraud decides the right thing is to flee quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command or verb meaning to leave in a hurry, beat a hasty retreat.

clue.text: Kingdom observing genuine start to millennium

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of millennium

explanation.surface: A kingdom witnesses the true dawn of a new thousand years.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Hope to catch the rest being late, and serve dinner?

parts.note: a lie-in is a rest in bed later than usual in the morning
to wait at table is to serve a meal

explanation.surface: A waiter who overslept hopes to catch up and still serve dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to stay hidden ready to ambush, hoping to catch someone.

clue.text: Finally join writer: leaving defence HQ

indicators.note: leaving means the writer departs from the headquarters word

parts.note: the Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense
a pen is a writer, an instrument for writing

explanation.surface: At last join a writer as he quits the defence headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag on is to attach at the end, joining something finally.

clue.text: Con the chief this month

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish chief or commander
inst. (instant) is the old commercial abbreviation for this month

explanation.surface: Defraud the boss within the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a verb meaning swindle; it is the noun or preposition from pros and cons. INST is old letter-writing shorthand for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Con as in pros and cons means an argument opposed, the same sense as being in opposition.

clue.text: Bars introducing 25 as complaints procedure?

definitions.meaning: a fence made of bars, as round a park or balcony
with entry 25 after it, the word forms a phrase for complaining bitterly about something

explanation.surface: Pubs bring in a new grievance process.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs 25 across after it: to rail against something is to complain fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a barrier of bars; railing against a thing is protesting about it angrily.

clue.text: Book sent for my attention

definitions.meaning: what an envelope addressed to the speaker would say: directed at the speaker

explanation.surface: A volume posted to me personally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a big scholarly book; split in two it is the phrase for something addressed to the speaker.

clue.text: Jack's approach isn't quite on the level here, in the end

definitions.text: Jack's approach isn't quite on the level here, in the end

parts.words: Jack's approach isn't quite on the level here, in the end
parts.note: in the game of bowls the small target ball rolls over a lawn that rises to a hump in the middle, so it is not flat

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is not entirely honest in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is not a man but the small target ball in bowls; 'on the level' means flat ground, not honest. A crown green is a bowling lawn raised in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown green is a bowling green that rises in the middle, so the approach to the target ball is never level.
